lines: I remember my mind working again, like a tool freed from rust.
You put a handle back on my life when I could not grip it myself.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember cold, hunger, and then your face cutting through the fog.
Being cured was not like waking up. I came back piece by piece.
Some part of me still listens for that old <shake>groan</shake>. I hate that part.
You helped me back. I may not say it gracefully, but I know what that means.
The village feels brighter now that I can notice it again.
I owe you more than a trade discount. We both know that.
Do not make a ceremony of it. Just know I remember.
The first tool I picked up afterward felt familiar. That nearly made me cry.
You stayed long enough for the cure to work. Thank you.
I can stand at my bench again because you did not give up on me.
The smell of iron was the first ordinary thing I recognized.
I remember hearing your voice before I understood the words.
Every normal morning since then feels borrowed in the best way.
My hands are steady again. I have you to thank for that.
You gave me the chance to be myself again.
I still have bad nights, but I wake up as myself and I am home.
If you ever need a repair, bring it to me first.
Your face fits the memory, though the memory is still badly forged.
I remember the cure hurting, then my thoughts slowly returning.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
Were you there with the potion? I think you were.
I know I have seen you before. The room was darker then.
There is a gap in my memory where your voice should be.
I remember hands holding me still. One pair may have been yours.
The cure comes back in <shake>flashes</shake>. Your face is in more than one.
I cannot place every moment, but I know you helped.
Forgive me if I ask again. Some names still will not stay put.
I remember the taste of the apple more clearly than the hours around it.
Part of me recognizes you before the rest catches up.
Did you carry me inside? I keep seeing a doorway behind you.
The memories return out of order. Today I remembered your boots.
I know I should thank you. I only wish I knew exactly what for.
Your voice makes the missing pieces feel closer.
I recall the weakness afterward and someone bringing me water.
Please be patient. The cure fixed more than my memory can explain.
I remember trusting you before I remembered why.
Whatever happened, I woke safe. That is enough to thank you.
I remember you. The old fear still catches like a nicked blade.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Please do not come closer yet. I am trying to stay calm.
Your face belongs to both the rescue and the nightmare.
I believe you mean no harm. My body has not learned that yet.
The sound of a potion bottle still makes me flinch.
Thank you for the cure. Give me time with everything else.
I remember snapping at you through the bars. The memory feels too close.
Stay by the door for now. I need a clear way out.
I can speak with you, but I cannot pretend I feel safe yet.
Some days I remember your help. Other days I only remember being trapped.
Do not touch me without warning. Not even to help.
I know that was not truly me, but I still lived through it.
Your footsteps bring back more than I want them to.
I am grateful. I am also <shake>afraid</shake>. Both are true.
Let me keep the bench between us while we talk.
The cure worked. Trust will take longer.
I need quiet more than questions right now.
Come back another day. I may be steadier then.
